key_insight: Integrating DMAIC with two-level Fuzzy AHP identified defects as the dominant waste and Machine, Method, and Man as the leading potential cause categories in robotic sidebeam bogie-frame welding.
engineering_relevance: The findings guide improvement priorities toward seam-tracking verification, robot parameter standardization, fixture positioning, tack welding, and fit-up control.
method: DMAIC baseline assessment using VSM, time study, u′-control chart, DPMO, and sigma analysis.
Two-level Fuzzy AHP using judgments from 10 experts to prioritize waste and potential cause categories.
6M fishbone analysis and corrective-action records to develop an improvement roadmap.
evidence_signal: Across 21 inspected units, 485 welding defects yielded 136,658.21 DPMO and a 2.60 sigma level; undercut represented 57.1% of defects, and process cycle efficiency was 4.88%.
watch_item: Weak expert agreement and sensitivity to respondent selection limit confidence in the rankings; proposed improvements still require implementation and empirical validation.
paper_title: Integration of DMAIC and Two-Level Fuzzy AHP for Diagnosing and Prioritizing Waste and Potential Causes of Welding Defects in a Sidebeam Bogie Frame
